title: Agglutinated protist shells form by surface energy, not choice or skill

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Agglutinated protist shells form by surface energy, not choice or skill

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The building of agglutinated shells from sand-grains, spicules or diatom frustules by rhizopods such as Difflugia is a purely physical consequence of foreign particles being trapped in the surface film by surface energy, with selectivity explained by specific surface-energies rather than volition.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The formation of an “agglutinated” shell is thus seen to be a purely physical phenomenon, and indeed a special case of a more general physical phenomenon which has many other important consequences in biology.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Agglutinated shells of rhizopods”. Scope: agglutinated testate amoebae and foraminifera

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-13: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism can be formalized, but 'purely physical' requires excluding active biological processes. Existing images of agglutinated tests lack the simultaneous behavioral and interfacial measurements needed for that discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate particle incorporation probabilities to particle size, shape, chemistry and measured interfacial energies in time-lapse observations of shell building. A surface-energy model must predict selectivity and assembly without organismal transport behavior better than active-choice models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Surface energy is not usually measured alongside particle-selection behavior.

Active cytoskeletal transport and passive trapping can coexist.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Foreign particles in the test are observable, but volition versus surface energy is not a unique pattern in grain counts. Sediment and foraminiferal census data are public, while the particle-by-particle composition of tests is not systematically attached to them. Existing studies can test a subset of rhizopods and leave the mechanism underdetermined.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the grains in agglutinated tests with the surrounding sediment for size, shape and mineralogy, and ask whether the bias matches specific surface energies. A bias predicted by surface energy supports the physical account; a selectivity that surface energy does not predict is at least compatible with active choice.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Grain preference is predicted both by surface energy and by biological selection, so the same bias fits both.

Matched test-plus-sediment measurements are scattered in papers rather than linked in one archive.
